frontier.reverified: RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-05 (neiso-84) ON THE DESIGNATED KEEPER'S OWN COMMITTED SIDECARS -- NO SOLVE, NO RUN PRODUCED, committed artifacts only. THE DECLARATION HOLDS; nothing is re-declared and no mechanism was tested. This SUPERSEDES the neiso-82 (2026-08-04) re-verification, which reached the same conclusion on the same load-bearing check but read two secondary numbers off the wrong pass -- see (3) below. (1) THE LOAD-BEARING CHECK PASSES ON THIS RUN'S OWN DATA, not by inheritance. hourly/reserve_family_<year>.parquet -- the ONLY artifact in which a locational reserve family's binding is observable (system's reserve_price is the cross-family SUM broadcast identically to every zone) -- carries shortfall_mw = 0.0 and held_mw >= requirement in EVERY one of 157,680 family-hours (3 years x 8,760 h x 3 families x 2 persisted passes), at exactly the published static requirements (ne_30min_total 1,800 / ne_10min_total 1,200 / ne_10min_spin 600 MW). NO HOUR GOES RESERVE-SHORT, so the frontier basis has NOT moved and the in-LP ISO-NE RCPF co-optimization remains DORMANT. PRECISION CORRECTION to the neiso-82 wording: the dual is NOT bit-zero on this keeper. 3 of the 157,680 family-hours carry a nonzero ne_30min_total dual -- 1 in 2024 and 2 in 2025 -- of magnitude <= 2.84e-14 $/MWh, i.e. $0.00 to any displayable precision and with zero shortfall in every one. They are LP degeneracy noise, not a binding: the prior keeper (neiso81_chpheatrate_B) and neiso-83's own zero-delta control arm are both bit-zero, so the three appear WITH the cc_steam_part_reclass arm. 'reserve dual $0.00, no hour reserve-short' is exact; 'min = max = -0.0, zero exceptions' is not, and is corrected here rather than carried. The neiso-82 text also said 'in BOTH P0 and P1'; the sidecar's own pass labels are 'P1' and 'P2'. (2) THE LEDGERED C3c CAVEAT'S SIZING AND WORDING RE-VERIFY AND STAND. From this keeper's own hourly/system_<year>.parquet on the SCORED pass, model hours > $300/MWh = 0 in all three years on BOTH an any-zone and a load-weighted basis (and 0 on the other pass too, so the count is basis-independent). The determination reproduces byte-for-byte via scripts/calibration_verdict.py --run-id: CALIBRATED-WITH-CAVEATS, 0 FAILs, 1 ledgered C3c caveat, C1 all 12/12 free 8/8, C7 unscored-protective. (3) TWO CARRIED-FORWARD NUMBERS WERE READ OFF THE NON-SCORED PASS AND ARE CORRECTED IN PLACE (no re-solve). THIS BUNDLE PERSISTS TWO PASSES, 'P1' AND 'P2', AND IS SCORED ON 'P2'. The recipe carries meta.json commitment=true, so run_year's legacy commitment pass ran and the final dispatch it returns -- persisted as 'P2' -- is what the registered run payload was rendered from. Verified two independent ways: HQ_import mean LMP matches P2 to 4 dp in all three years (P1 off by 0.058/0.013/0.041 $/MWh), and the 2025 payload's coal 0.21 TWh / gas 61.35 TWh match P2's 0.2108/61.3457 rather than P1's 0.2159/61.3427. Consequently the SCORED-pass annual maxima are $249.50 / $256.93 / $280.85, not the $248.97 / $218.24 / $280.85 neiso-82 recorded; its correction of the 2024 figure from a stale '~$204' to '$218.24' was itself wrong-basis and is superseded by $256.93 in the keeper's calibration_attestation.json. (4) THE SHARPENING OBSERVATION SURVIVES AND STRENGTHENS ON THE SCORED PASS, and one leg of neiso-82's reading of it is reversed. The model's closest approach to the tail threshold is SUMMER in all three years: 2025-06-24/25 at $280.85 (93.6 % of $300, ON the DA-visible heat-wave event the caveat names), 2024-07-15 17:00 at $256.93 (85.6 %), 2023-09-07 16-17h at $249.50 (83.2 %); scored-pass winter maxima are $233.87 / $198.52 / $232.92. But 2024's single closest hour sits $1.07 UNDER the ~$258 dual-fuel oil-parity cap -- so in the model's tightest 2024 hour that cap IS effectively the wall, which is the OPPOSITE of neiso-82's reading ('the cap is not the binding constraint in the hours the model comes closest'), reached because it read the non-scored pass's $218.24. This sharpens the note's existing pointer that the remaining C3c distance is summer peak-load-margin offer formation (its own charter); it does not overturn the declaration and NO C3c LEVER WAS RE-OPENED (rule 28a). (5) OPEN FOR THE OWNER, NOT ACTED ON HERE. NEISO is the ONLY ISO of six that runs the archived P2 commitment pass: all 15 committed NEISO bundles carry meta.json commitment=true, all 111 bundles of the other five ISOs carry commitment=false. CLAUDE.md 'Dispatch & Commitment' states P0/P1 are the only production passes, every run is scored on P1, and no keeper uses P2. The --commitment CLI flag has been hard-gated behind --enable-legacy-p2 since 2026-08-03, but run_replay_bundle re-injects a recipe's flags from meta.json AFTER that gate runs on parsed CLI args, so every replay carries the P2 pass forward invisibly -- which is how neiso-83 ran it. Materiality is small but non-zero (2025 COAL_BIT 0.2159 -> 0.2108 TWh, -2.3 %; mean LMP +0.058/+0.011/+0.038 $/MWh; the 2024 annual max +18 %). Resolving it needs a re-solve and is therefore out of scope for a no-run re-verification session; it is escalated, not silently corrected, and the determination as scored is unaffected. (6) C2 STILL WAITS: the 2025 EIA-923 vintage has NOT landed (re-checked this session with --no-write; NEISO's committed block reproduces byte-identically, CC_CHP and CC_REGULAR incomplete at 57 % reporting, every class gate=false), so the 2025 C1 CC rows stay SKIPPED and nothing was estimated around it. note: neiso-83 (2026-08-05) arms cc_steam_part_reclass at NEISO -- a CLASSIFICATION-CORRECTNESS fix with ZERO free parameters, promoted on rules 1 [R-STRUCT] / 13 [R-MEASURED] / 14 [R-ACCURATE] and explicitly NOT on a score. It is a replay_keeper re-solve of the 2026-08-04-neiso81-chpheatrate recipe with EXACTLY ONE DELTA (a programmatic diff of the two scenario blocks returns the single key cc_steam_part_reclass), scored against a SAME-HEAD ZERO-DELTA CONTROL (2026-08-05-neiso-83-control-zerodelta) rather than against the committed keeper (miso-124). THAT CONTROL CAME BACK BYTE-IDENTICAL to the committed keeper -- max |class-hour delta| 0.000000 MW in all three years -- so unlike neiso-81 there is NO same-HEAD drift to decompose and every arm-B number is the mechanism. WHAT THE DEFECT WAS. EIA-860 6081 Stony Brook CA1 is the STEAM half of a 3x1 combined-cycle block. The LP carried it as a 96.0 MW standalone `oil` generator (VOM $4.50, 1.0 t-CO2/MWh, EFORd 0.10) while its three combustion-turbine siblings sat in CC_REGULAR/gas_cc (VOM $2.00, 0.43, 0.05) sharing its heat rate exactly. A combined-cycle steam turbine HAS NO COMBUSTION PATH -- it runs on HRSG exhaust, reports no CEMS stack (plant 6081 meters five units in every train year and none of them is CA1), and every MMBtu the block burns is already metered at those siblings. The model was burning distillate in a machine with no fuel of its own. WHY EIA-860'S `DFO` LABEL IS NOT THE MACHINE'S FUEL, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED. EIA-923 Page 1 reports the CA row's OWN fuel split, and it tracks its CT siblings' split year by year across a 0.004 -> 0.468 swing in the block's oil share (|gap| 0.0016-0.0217, 2018-2022): the steam part inherits whatever the block burned. `DFO` on that row is a duct / legacy code. WHY IT IS NOT DOUBLE-COUNTING THE BLOCK'S FUEL. The incumbent heat rate is the eGRID PLANT-AVERAGE, whose PLNGENAN denominator already counts the steam part's own generation -- a BLOCK rate. Applying it uniformly to every block MW reproduces the block's total fuel burn by construction; the UNARMED state is the inconsistent one, charging a block-denominated rate to 209.1 MW of a 305.1 MW block and pricing the missing 96 MW off the distillate curve. Capacity is UNCHANGED (24,209.58 MW both arms) -- class, fuel, VOM, CO2 rate and EFORd move, and the heat rate does not. WHY A NEW FLAG AND NOT cc_steam_part_capacity. That mechanism only RESTORES rows the fuel map DROPS; a CARRIED row is outside its population entirely, which is why neiso-80 measured a byte-identical armed fleet and stamped it `I`. Its `fuel_type is None` gate is load-bearing (miso-125 s6 -- it is what keeps MISO 1004 Edwardsport's real 555 MW IGCC machine in COAL), so re-classing gets its own flag and its own ISO registry. cc_steam_part_capacity is NOT re-armed and its `I` is NOT re-stamped (rule 28a). LIVENESS AT TWO GRAINS (miso-126a -- a fleet-loader check alone is NOT proof): grain 1, a pre-arm fleet rebuild at THIS keeper's own ScenarioConfig moves EXACTLY ONE unit of 431 with total pmax conserved to the milli-MW; grain 2, the post-arm per-class ENERGY delta is oil -0.00231 / -0.00034 / -0.00139 TWh against CC_REGULAR +0.00220 / +0.00062 / +0.01078 TWh for 2023/24/25. A byte-identical arm would have scored INVALID, not inert. RULE 25 [R-ISO-SCOPE] PROVEN BY RUNNING IT: with the flag armed, the ERCOT (1,450), CAISO (782), PJM (1,922), MISO (1,975) and NYISO (460) fleets are byte-identical, and MISO's Edwardsport -- the one other member of the national re-class population -- stays COAL. PRE-REGISTERED IN NUMBERS BEFORE EITHER ARM SOLVED: results/calibration/PREREG-neiso83-stonybrook-ca1-2026-08-05.md.
disposition_note: DETERMINATION CALIBRATED-WITH-CAVEATS, verified IDENTICAL rather than merely compatible: the same 1 ledgered caveat (C3c price tail / scarcity, RT hourly), the same unscored-protective C7 shape, 0 FAILs, and the same C1 headline (all 12/12, free 8/8) -- criterion for criterion identical to BOTH the superseded 2026-08-04-neiso81-chpheatrate keeper AND this session's own same-HEAD zero-delta control, which is what makes the A/B like-for-like. NO NEW CAVEAT SLOT IS SPENT and the 2026-07-11 frontier declaration is untouched -- C3c is bit-unchanged (model 0 >$300 hours in both arms, all three years). NONE of the four pre-registered stop-and-escalate triggers fires. RULE 22 D-5(b) SATISFIED AND NOT MERELY ASSERTED: the re-verified determination is NOT worse, so this promotion proceeds without an owner escalation. (i) THE RESULT IS CORRECT AND NUMERICALLY SMALL, AND THAT IS REPORTED AS A CLEAN OUTCOME, NOT APOLOGISED FOR (rule 1 [R-STRUCT]: a structurally correct mechanism stays in whether or not the residual moves). Largest class move is CC_REGULAR +0.0108 TWh in 2025 = 0.018 % of the class; load-weighted lambda moves +0.0005 / -0.0192 / -0.0701 $/MWh (+0.001 % / -0.04 % / -0.10 % of level); summed per-class C1 |error| delta is +0.0044 / -0.0004 / -0.0010 TWh, i.e. marginally worse in 2023 and marginally better in 2024 and 2025, all of it two orders of magnitude inside the +/-1.955-2.103 TWh C1 band. (ii) WHY THE REALIZED EFFECT IS ~1/100th OF THE AVAILABLE HEADROOM, measured rather than hand-waved: 6081's heat rate of 10.6062 MMBtu/MWh sits above 97.5 % of NEISO's CC_REGULAR capacity (cap-weighted p50 7.340, p90 8.616; only 312.1 MW of the class is dearer). The re-classed 96 MW is deep out of merit and clears only in the tightest hours -- which is also why the 2025 move is absorbed almost exactly by CT_PEAKER (-0.0111 TWh against CC_REGULAR +0.0108). (iii) THE CHARTER'S OWN MAGNITUDE EXPECTATION WAS CORRECTED BEFORE THE SOLVE, NOT AFTER. The lane was chartered expecting '< 0.15 % of CC_REGULAR'. Phase 0 measured the block's effective available capacity moving 0.0 -> 0.0 / 61.7 -> 156.4 / 40.5 -> 134.2 MW (2023/24/25) -- materially more HEADROOM than that -- and the prereg said so in advance. The realized DISPATCH effect then came in an order of magnitude UNDER the charter's bound, for reason (ii). Both halves are on the record. (iv) THE DENOMINATOR LEG IS PART OF THIS MECHANISM AND WAS DISCLOSED IN ADVANCE. The CAMPD unit-outage overlay derates (plant_code, plant_group) by removed_mw / plant_capacity_mw and reads that denominator off the same fleet, so it moves with the flag (209.1 -> 305.1 MW at 6081). Un-forwarded it would remove the wrong ABSOLUTE MW -- a 152 MW 2024 outage against the un-armed denominator removes 72.7 % of an armed 305.1 MW bin = 221.8 MW, 46 % more than went out. Decomposed at Phase 0: capacity leg +0.0 / +28.3 / +18.6 MW against denominator leg +0.0 / +66.4 / +75.2 MW. Rule 23 [R-FROZEN-DERIVE] is NOT engaged -- the outage deriver's own inputs at 6081 are identical under both arms, so the committed extract would re-derive byte-for-byte, and nothing was regenerated. (v) OPEN ROOT-CAUSE ISSUE, NAMED AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED (rules 19 / 21 / 25). campd-unit-outages-NEISO.csv carries plant 6081's DIESEL peakers (CAMPD units 004/005 = EIA-860 generators 1 and 2) with plant_group=CC_REGULAR, because `oil` carries no plant_group at all and the overlay cannot represent an oil unit's outage. In 2024 and 2025 those two units are the ONLY source of 6081 outage rows while the CC block's own units 001/002/003 have none -- so the model derates a fully-available CC block to 29.5 % / 19.4 %. Pre-existing, ISO-agnostic, and a fleet-taxonomy change with six-ISO blast radius. The armed denominator moves the block TOWARD physical truth, not away from it, which is why rule 14 says take the consistent basis and open the root cause rather than bury it in an inconsistent one. (vi) THE BENCHMARK SIDE IS NOT SYMMETRICALLY CORRECTED, and the residue is measured rather than assumed: the EIA-923 benchmark buckets Page-1 rows through the same classify_plant registry but at NATIONAL scope with no ISO gate, so re-classing there would reach MISO's Edwardsport. The un-corrected residue is the 6081 CA/DFO row -- 2,165 MWh in 2023 and ZERO in 2024 and 2025, i.e. 0.0022 TWh against a +/-1.955 TWh C1 band (0.11 % of it). cc_steam_part_capacity's own MISO keeper does not touch the benchmark side either. (vii) CARRIED FORWARD UNCHANGED from the superseded keeper and still true: CC_CHP sits UNDER actual in every year where it sat over -- a real, ungated and currently unclosable residual whose only named route is CLOSED WITH EVIDENCE by neiso-71 -- and the 2025 C1 CC rows stay SKIPPED on the preliminary EIA-923 vintage (re-checked this session, still not landed).
